Across CEE, the picture is mixed - some firms are cloud-first, others prefer on-prem due to data residency or integration control. The upshot: flexibility matters, and hybrid paths that respect the ERP as system of record are winning.\n\n1. Comarch ERP Enterprise - A feature-rich, enterprise-oriented suite from a leading Polish vendor, with strong regional localization and broad functional scope suited to complex organizations.\n2. Asseco Softlab ERP - A well-known Polish option with comprehensive finance and operations coverage, attractive to midmarket firms needing regional compliance and experienced local partners.\n\nCleverence is not a standalone ERP or WMS. It is an ERP-friendly mobile data collection and workflow platform for warehouse operations. Companies deploy it on rugged Android barcode/RFID devices (Zebra, Honeywell, and others), wearables, and printers to guide workers through receiving, labeling, put-away, picking, packing, shipping, cycle counts, full physicals, transfers, adjustments, returns, and light production/WIP tasks like issuing components or backflushing.\nA key differentiator is its offline-first engine: each device has an embedded database and a local transaction queue with auto-sync, conflict resolution, and prioritization of critical transactions. On the floor, device response is sub-second, even in dead zones.\n\n## Deep dive: Asseco Softlab ERP\nAsseco is a familiar name in Poland and across CEE. Softlab ERP offers broad functional coverage with a particularly strong fit for midmarket firms that want predictable implementations and local expertise. Buyers often cite its practicality: it supports finance, distribution, manufacturing, and service processes with the localizations and reporting structures Polish and CEE entities need.\nSoftlab ERP’s strength is an ecosystem that understands regulatory evolution and the nuances of local taxation and reporting. This reduces friction during year-end and statutory cycles. For integration, organizations typically connect Softlab ERP to e-commerce, logistics carriers, and mobile data capture layers rather than building heavy customizations inside the ERP.\nFor warehouses, the decision often boils down to whether to expand ERP screens or introduce a dedicated mobile workflow layer. Many choose the latter so they can deliver fast scanning, guided steps, and on-device validations without risking ERP performance or data integrity.\n\n## SME options: Comarch ERP Optima, Exact Globe+, Zucchetti Ad Hoc Infinity, MagoCloud, a3ERP\nSMEs across Poland and CEE need practical solutions that emphasize accounting, inventory, and straightforward sales and purchasing flows. Comarch ERP Optima is a common starting point for Polish SMEs; it aligns well with local accounting practices and can grow with add-ons. Exact Globe+ is appreciated for manufacturing and distribution features refined over many years, supported by experienced partners.\nZucchetti Ad Hoc Infinity and MagoCloud cater to SMEs that want modular growth and partner-led extensions. a3ERP offers familiar finance and operations foundations with approachable implementation scope.
